headlines.title: Preliminary 4.1 magnitude and 4.5 magnitude quakes strike in Northern California
headlines.description: A preliminary 4.1 magnitude earthquake followed by a preliminary 4.5 magnitude struck in Northern California, according to the United States Geological Survey. The first quake, with preliminary magnitude of 4.1, hit at 3:20 p.m. and was centered 19.26 miles northwest of Covelo and approximately 210 miles north of San Francisco, the USGS said. According to the USGS, a second earthquake, with a preliminary magnitude of 4.5, hit a minute later and was centered in the same area. The temblors come after the Covelo area was rattled by a 4.0 magnitude earthquake on Tuesday. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates. headlines.title: Deadly mass shooting near Morgan Hill: FBI joins investigation, offers $20K reward
headlines.description: The FBI has joined the investigation into last month’s deadly mass shooting at a pop-up birthday party near Morgan Hill and is offering a reward of up to $20,000 for information leading to an arrest, the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office said Wednesday. Seven people were shot, one fatally, during the party on Saturday, July 25, at a rural property along Hale Avenue, officials said. The party, which was advertised on social media, drew hundreds of attendees. The sheriff’s office said the FBI’s involvement in the investigation will bring “significant federal resources and technical support” into play as authorities work to identify the person or persons responsible. “With hundreds of people in attendance, someone knows something,” Santa Clara County Sheriff Robert Jonsen said in a statement. “We’ve asked for the FBI’s assistance, and we are calling on our community to help identify those responsible for this heinous crime. We are grateful the FBI is stepping forward and encouraging others to do the same.” Anyone who was in the area at the time of the shooting and captured photos, videos or other forms of digital content is encouraged to upload their files via the FBI’s digital media tip line. “Those responsible for this senseless shooting should know that the FBI and our law enforcement partners at the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office will use every available resource to identify and hold them accountable,” FBI San Francisco Special Agent in Charge Scott Schelble said in a statement. “The FBI is offering a reward of up to $20,000 because we believe someone has information that can help move this investigation forward. No piece of information is too small, and your tip could make a difference in bringing justice to the victims, their families, and the Morgan Hill community.” Anyone with additional information about the shooting is asked to call the FBI at 1‑800‑CALL‑FBI. headlines.title: 5 arrested in San Francisco child predator sting
headlines.description: Editor’s note: This story was updated to reflect revised arrest numbers provided by authorities. Five people were arrested, not seven. The San Francisco Sheriff’s Office and District Attorney’s Office announced the arrests of five men following a three-day undercover operation targeting suspected child predators. The operation, conducted with the help of 10 other law enforcement agencies, took place over three days at the end of July. During the investigation, officers posed as children on several online platforms. Authorities said seven men contacted the undercover investigators seeking to meet for lewd acts. According to investigators, four of the men showed up to meet who they believed were children but were instead met by law enforcement officers. The five men arrested are from San Francisco, San Mateo, Daly City and Redwood City. The four men facing felony charges remain in custody. Sheriff Paul Miyamoto and District Attorney Brooke Jenkins urged parents to use available tools to limit their children’s interactions with strangers online and to have conversations about the dangers of online grooming. “They are very clearly exploitative in nature, very clearly not appropriate relations between an adult and a minor,” Miyamoto said. “You need to be monitoring what those conversations are. You need to be talking to your children about talking to strangers,” Jenkins said. “They think about talking to strangers in person, but we need to talk to them about the dangers of talking to strangers online.” Parents looking for resources on how to protect children online can find information through the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force at icactaskforce.org.

headlines.title: Several San Ramon businesses burglarized
headlines.description: San Ramon police were investigating a series of business burglaries that happened early Tuesday morning. Police said officers initially responded at about 4:10 a.m. to Utopia Tanning Salon regarding a glass break alarm. While on the scene, several other burglaries were discovered, police said. Other affected businesses included The Saffron Grill, Club Pilates, Pizza My Heart and Supercuts. Surveillance footage of the break-ins was being examined by police in hopes of finding leads on possible suspects, police said. Anyone with information is asked to call police at 925-973-2779.

headlines.title: Alameda County settles with family of 8-year-old killed in child abuse case
headlines.description: Alameda County reached a settlement with the family of an 8-year-old girl who died after child welfare allegedly failed to intervene in her neglect and abuse by her mother. “Sophia Mason was an 8-year-old girl who deserved protection and a full life,” the Alameda County Board of Supervisors said in a statement on behalf of the entire board Tuesday. “We mourn with her grandmother and extended family for what could have been.” Sophia died in her Merced home in 2022, a year after being taken into the custody of her mother. Throughout this time, Alameda County received seven emergency hotline referrals saying Sophia was suffering abuse at home, according to a legal claim filed by attorneys representing her grandmother. In 2023, Sophia’s mother pleaded guilty to voluntary manslaughter, child abuse and causing great bodily injury in connection with her death. As part of the settlement, the county will pay $12 million to Sylvia Johnson, Sophia’s grandmother, and dedicate a park bench to Sophia. The county also commissioned an independent investigation into its failures handling Sophia’s case that led to 25 suggestions for reform. Among the deficiencies found in the resulting report was that social workers did not respond to and investigate all allegations of suspected child abuse or neglect. Child welfare workers also failed to cross-report to law enforcement, despite being mandated reporters. Miranda Counseling & Consulting, which was contracted for the investigation, proposed greater oversight, injury documentation and internal auditing. Alameda County’s Social Services Agency will “undergo extensive new training, be held to new documentation standards, and new accountability for oversight and accuracy in safety and risk assessments,” supervisors wrote in the statement.

headlines.title: San Bruno Post Office robbery: Public told to check financial accounts, $150K reward issued
headlines.description: The U.S. Postal Inspection Service is offering a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the person or people who stole mail from the San Bruno Post Office last week. The robbery at the post office, located at 1300 Huntington Ave., happened between 4:55 p.m. and 5:10 p.m. last Thursday, officials said. At least one person entered the post office, took four tubs of mail and assaulted a postal employee, according to officials. “If you recently visited the San Bruno Post Office or deposited mail into a collection box serviced by that office — including collection boxes in the South San Francisco area — your mail may have been affected,” San Bruno police said in a post on social media. Police said residents should monitor their financial accounts for any unauthorized activity. Those who believe their mail may have been stolen or compromised are instructed to file a report with the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (reference case No. 4750763-ROBB). Anyone with information about the robbery is encouraged to contact the U.S. Postal Inspection Service at 1-877-876-2455.

headlines.title: Outside Lands 2026: Performers, food vendors, activities and what to know
headlines.description: The annual three-day San Francisco music festival, Outside Lands, kicks off Friday. Here’s what to know ahead of the highly-anticipated event. Where will Outside Lands be held? The festival will be held at Golden Gate Park and will host over 90 artists and 100 food and drink vendors. San Francisco 19 hours ago San Francisco May 6 Who is performing at Outside Lands? Headliners include Charli XCX, The Strokes, PinkPanthress, Rüfüs Du Sol and Empire of the Sun. Other performers include Labyrinth, GloRilla, Djo and Geese. The earliest acts begin at 12 p.m. each day and the latest performances will start at 10 p.m. Visit the schedule page to view all performers and their set times. What will the food menu offer at Outside Lands? Various food and drink locations will also be available at the festival. Locations are spread across the festival with options for multiple dietary restrictions. Special drink locations at the festival include Cocktail Magic, Wine Lands and Beer Lands. Visit the full list of food and drink options on Outside Land’s website. Outside Lands transportation: What to know Transportation is another factor that the festival urges fans to consider. There is no general admission parking at the festival. Outside Lands recommends that festivalgoers leave their cars at home and utilize public transportation. The festival offers shuttle passes, picking up fans from Bill Graham Civic Auditorium in San Francisco. Other modes of transportation to consider include Muni, BART, and rideshare services. Outside Lands bag policy Festivalgoers are also warned about Outside Lands bag policy. The following bag types are allowed, per Outside Lands webpage: Backpacks and bags made of clear plastic, clear vinyl, or clear PVC Small bags, fanny-packs, purses up to 6” x 8” x 3” (do not have to be clear) Empty dedicated hydration packs with a bladder capacity of under 2.5 liters or 150 inches, and no more than one additional pocket. Standard size backpacks with hydration bladders will not be permitted. Other FAQ answers are available to view in the information section. Are tickets still available for Outside Lands? Limited tickets remain and are at a high resale price. To secure legitimate tickets, Outside Lands provides access to their Official Resale Marketplace. If you are unable to visit the festival in person, it will be streamed on Amazon Music, Prime Video, Twitch, Fire TV and Samsung TV Plus. headlines.title: Major closures coming to Carquinez Bridge
headlines.description: Major closures are coming to the Carquinez Bridge, which connects Vallejo to the East Bay. The bridge is set for a full deck replacement. Caltrans said crews need to repave the bridge to ensure safety and smoothness. Crews will begin repairs at 6 p.m. Friday, resulting in one westbound lane closure. The repair is expected to continue until 7 p.m. Saturday. A full bridge closure will start two weeks later on Aug. 21. Lanes will reopen on Aug. 24.

headlines.title: AC/DC set to hit the stage at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara
headlines.description: AC/DC will take the stage at Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara Wednesday night. Crews have been preparing the stadium for fans and band members, who are now in their 70s. While fans gear up for the concert, pop-up events are being hosted in the Bay Area. The Hard Rock Cafe at Fisherman’s Wharf in San Francisco is hosting a special pop-up store, providing fans with tour items and memorabilia that cannot be found anywhere else.

headlines.title: Businesses in San Jose's Branham Plaza burglarized
headlines.description: At least six stores at Branham Plaza in San Jose were burglarized Monday night, according to business owners. The strip mall is located at Pearl Avenue and Branham Lane, not far from Capitol Expressway. It wasn’t immediately known what was stolen from the businesses. Crews were busy Tuesday boarding up glass doors and windows that were damaged by the vandals. Meanwhile, San Jose police were searching for who was responsible for the string of burglaries.

headlines.title: Man convicted of burning Jewish scroll at Berkeley religious study center
headlines.description: A jury has convicted a 45-year-old man of arson after he used a pocket torch to burn a Jewish religious scroll at the entrance of a Berkeley study center in February, the Alameda County District Attorney’s Office said. Jurors found David William Denton guilty of arson in connection with the Feb. 6 blaze at a religious study center on Bancroft Way, where authorities said he vandalized and set fire to a mezuzah scroll attached to a doorway. The fire damaged the religious item, prosecutors said Tuesday. Following the verdict, a judge ordered Denton into custody pending sentencing. He faces a maximum sentence of three years in state prison and will be required to register as an arson offender if sentenced, prosecutors said. “Targeting and burning a sacred religious symbol is an act that can cause harm far beyond the physical damage itself,” District Attorney Ursula Jones Dickson said in a statement. “People of every faith should be able to practice their religion and gather in their communities without fear of intimidation.” Denton will be sentenced on Sept. 3.

headlines.title: Walnut Creek house fire leaves 1 person injured, 2 dogs dead
headlines.description: Fire crews with the Contra Costa County Fire Protection District fought a two-alarm house fire in Walnut Creek on Tuesday afternoon that injured one person and killed two dogs. The call came in at 3:39 p.m. reporting a fire in a single-family residence in the 700 block of Woodwind Place in Walnut Creek, according to Con Fire. Crews arrived to find visible flames and smoke and eventually a second alarm was called on the blaze. The fire was knocked down by 4:30 p.m., but as of 5:30 p.m., firefighters were still at the scene handling hot spots and other issues, Con Fire said. One person was transported to the hospital for smoke inhalation, according to Con Fire, but it is unclear if they were a resident of the home or a neighbor. Two dogs perished in the fire. The cause of the fire is still under investigation.
